SNDK.headline: Why Sandisk Investors Are Giving Thanks After Thanksgiving
SNDK.description: Sandisk stock surged 14% on Friday after falling 75% from June 2026 highs, driven by positive news from partner Kioxia demonstrating new solid-state memory chips that improve Nvidia GPU performance for AI functions. Despite concerns about NAND flash memory demand and AI growth sustainability, analysts forecast Sandisk will grow profits nearly 40% annually over the next five years, making the stock appear undervalued at 4x trailing earnings.

SNDK.headline: Western Digital vs. IBM: Which Data Storage Stock is the Smarter Bet?
SNDK.description: Western Digital (WDC) appears better positioned than IBM to capitalize on AI and cloud-driven data storage demand, posting 55% revenue growth with strong margins and upward earnings revisions. WDC trades at a lower valuation (8.97X forward earnings vs IBM's 18.5X) and carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating, while IBM's diversified enterprise software and hybrid cloud business offers more stability but slower growth momentum with a Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

SNDK.headline: Micron's Higher FY27 CapEx: Can Supply Security Boost Its Growth Further?
SNDK.description: Micron Technology is increasing fiscal 2027 capital expenditure to $25 billion in the first half to expand manufacturing capacity and meet AI-driven demand for memory products. New Idaho fabs and a Singapore HBM packaging facility are expected to strengthen supply security, with industry DRAM bit shipments projected to grow at low-20% rates in 2027-2028. However, higher spending carries execution risks including construction delays and potential oversupply.

SNDK.headline: Sandisk’s 8-for-1 Split Is Done. Here’s What Investors Should Do Next.
SNDK.description: Sandisk completed its 8-for-1 stock split on November 19, 2026, which doesn't change the company's value but makes shares more accessible. Long-term customer contracts covering half of fiscal 2027 supply and two-thirds of fiscal 2028 supply provide reassurance. SNDK.headline: Seagate Shares Tumble 46% in 6 months: Buy, Sell or Hold STX Now?
SNDK.description: Seagate Technology (STX) delivered strong fiscal Q1 results with 61% revenue growth and record free cash flow of $1.5 billion, driven by AI infrastructure and data center demand. However, the stock's 45.8% decline over six months, premium valuation at 9.95x forward P/E, and execution risks with HAMR technology adoption warrant a cautious approach. The company maintains a Hold rating despite healthy underlying business fundamentals.

SNDK.headline: 4 Memory and Storage Stocks Cut by More Than 30% That I'd Buy Now and Hold for the Next Decade
